title: Cap the length of a scored highlight
statement: Where a highlighted span earns credit by how much of a keyed span it covers, cap its length, since a whole-passage highlight covers every key.
example: A draft rule credits a span that covers at least half of a keyed span and caps it at three times that span's length.
detail: Drafting deterministic acceptance rules for a find-and-explain task, a reading project credited a student's selected span when it covered at least half of some keyed span. Because a whole-passage highlight would trivially meet that rule, the draft adds a guard: the student's span may be at most three times the length of the best-matching keyed span. The guard follows from scoring by coverage, so it applies wherever a free highlight is credited that way.
against: The draft marks its thresholds as uncalibrated proposals for Grade 3, and says the guard becomes unnecessary if the app ships sentence-level selection (`grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/tmp-g5-r8-src-scripts.tar.gz::scripts/lane-tools/drafts/m5-acceptance-rules.md`, lines 6-7 and 127-128).

evidence.quote: - SPAN-VALID: `r* >= 0.50` -- the student span covers at least half of some keyed span.
- SPAN-GUARD: student span length `<= 3 x` the length of the best-matching keyed span (blocks highlight-everything; a whole-passage highlight can trivially satisfy SPAN-VALID).
